abstract: We study two constrained routes toward larger rational Diophantine tuples: regular fifth completion of product-one square-product quadruples, and four-point translation orbits on elliptic curves induced by triples. For the first route, we derive a cubic necessary quotient, elliptic away from stated degeneracies. On a diagonal family, rank zero of an explicit elliptic curve excludes every nondegenerate regular completion retaining square products. Its torsion and lift analysis are uniform; elementary descent certifies three parameters, one supporting infinitely many valid starting quadruples. For the orbit route, two exact diagonal identities yield a uniform obstruction whenever the base product is a 2-adic unit. A rank-zero diagonal quotient forces a strong base product and a product-minus-one pair; an infinite nonunit branch has positive induced rank but is excluded by this quotient. A further rank-zero criterion filters entire families with fixed Pythagorean square-root ratios. We give a complete twelve-point reduced-case classification using an elementary elliptic descent. Finally, a rigorous interval L-value calculation resolves an explicit triple whose algebraic rank bounds were zero to two; modularity and the analytic-rank-zero theorem prove that it has exactly one nonzero common neighbor and cannot lie in a quintuple. Exact symbolic, congruence, group-law and interval certificates accompany the arguments. These results eliminate specified completion branches and demonstrate how to resolve a base unresolved by an initial algebraic descent. They neither exclude arbitrary irregular completions nor resolve the rational septuple problem.

coauthors.contribution: Developed the order-four orbit construction and special real obstruction and infinite nonunit positive-rank exclusion, supplied the regular survivor and fixed-ratio investigations, and independently reproduced the dyadic identities, elementary classifications, rigorous L-value certificate and torsion computations; reviewed the product-one argument and combined manuscript.
